metadata.document: SUBMISSION ON THE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT REFORM BILL

cleaned_body_text: The Environmental Defence Society (EDS) is a public interest environmental law group, formed in 1971. It has a membership that consists largely of resource management professionals. The focus of EDS’s work is on achieving good environmental outcomes through improving the quality of New Zealand’s legal and policy frameworks and statutory decision-making processes. EDS welcomes the opportunity to comment on the Resource Management Reform Bill (the Bill) which amends the Resource Management Act 1991 (RMA), Local Government (Auckland Transitional Provisions) Act 2010 (LGATPA), and the Local Government Official Information and Meetings Act 1987. This submission addresses amendments to section 76 of the RMA, section 32 of the RMA, and the LGATPA. EDS strongly opposes the proposed restrictions on district plan rules relating to tree protection. Trees provide important ecosystem services and amenity values. In cities the functions and values that trees fulfil cross boundaries. The retention of trees in urban environments is essential to meet the reasonably foreseeable needs of future generations and to safeguard the life-supporting capacity of air, water, soil and ecosystems. Local authorities require tools such as tree protection rules to achieve their statutory functions and give effect to higher-level instruments like the New Zealand Coastal Policy Statement. EDS has developed a compromise solution that distinguishes between trimming and removal, addresses trees in poor health, focuses on key groups of trees, and proposes effective methods for identification. EDS also supports improvements to section 32 reports but opposes amendments that draw undue attention to economic growth opportunity costs or introduce uncertainty. Regarding the LGATPA and the Auckland Unitary Plan, EDS has concerns regarding regulation-making powers, setting aside established RMA provisions, expert conferences, cross-examination, and the appointment and composition of the Hearings Panel. EDS requests that the proposed amendments to section 76 be rejected or modified, section 32 amendments be revised, and the Auckland Unitary Plan process be amended to address these concerns.
